source_claim: A paired micro-reproduction of a paper's claim-bearing intervention can predict cost-adjusted full-adoption utility on independently specified user tasks, with an explicit inconclusive region.

axes.problem: Decide cheaply whether adopting a paper intervention will benefit a user's task before full reproduction.
axes.mechanism: Same-scaffold intervention-versus-sham micro-runs, an independent task oracle, a cost-and-regression utility ledger, and an abstaining bridge to full-adoption outcomes.
axes.insight: Replication fidelity and artifact-local utility do not identify target-task net benefit; isolating the claim-bearing operator may provide a cheaper predictive contrast.
axes.application: Paper-derived agent skills and runnable paper methods on independently supplied user tasks.
axes.evaluation_scope: Selective sign accuracy, false-adoption rate, rank correlation, coverage, and calibration against held-out full-adoption outcomes.

comparisons.title: A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale
comparisons.evidence: The paper constructs tasks from skills and evaluates with-skill versus without-skill utility across agent-model configurations; it does not use independently supplied tasks or a same-scaffold operator sham to predict full-adoption net benefit.
comparisons.limitations: The overlap is material at the utility-evaluation level but not at the proposed paired micro-reproduction mechanism.

comparisons.title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
comparisons.evidence: PaperBench distinguishes code development, fresh execution, and result matching and reports a cheaper Code-Dev variant; its target is replication fidelity rather than target-task adoption utility.
comparisons.limitations: PaperBench directly bounds claims about first low-cost paper-reproduction evaluation.

comparisons.title: AutoReproduce: Automatic AI Experiment Reproduction with Paper Lineage
comparisons.evidence: AutoReproduce uses mini-batch and dry-run checks within end-to-end reproduction; these checks target executability and fidelity rather than isolated intervention benefit.
comparisons.limitations: It defeats any broad claim about rapid core-method reproduction.

comparisons.title: Cost-Sensitive Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization with Transfer of Learning Curve Extrapolation
comparisons.evidence: The abstract defines user cost-performance utility, predicts future performance from cheaper fidelities, and stops automatically; it assumes configurations on shared learning curves rather than heterogeneous paper interventions and paired target-task shams.
comparisons.limitations: Full text was not fetched in this run.

comparisons.title: A Unified Framework for the Transportability of Population-Level Causal Measures
comparisons.evidence: The abstract identifies and estimates target-population treatment effects under covariate shift, a direct conceptual ancestor of target-task benefit transfer.
comparisons.limitations: The candidate does not yet state transportability assumptions with comparable rigor.

limitations: Candidate-specific external collision terms were not transmitted; the assessment reuses generic run-scoped searches.
The eight-row local dataset is feasibility evidence, not adequate validation of calibration or cross-paper generalization.
